records.text: Everyday Heroes Like You initially funded and promoted transparent grassroots organizations, aiming to avoid charities that spent 70% on administration and only 30% on the cause.
records.speaker: Erika Kirk

appearances.snippet: I decided to create something called Everyday Heroes Like You, where we're able to originally, it was focused on bringing funds and awareness to various grassroots organizations that were in specific communities that would be able to have volunteers that are transparent with their funds that are actually doing what they're saying they're doing instead of just having 70% of the funds go to admin and only. only 30% towards the cause.

verification.notes: The episode transcript directly records Erika Kirk describing Everyday Heroes Like You's original focus on funding and awareness for transparent grassroots groups and contrasting that with 70/30 administrative spending. An independent nonprofit profile corroborates the organization's mission to assist and promote nonprofits globally.

records.text: Erika Kirk said that while living in China she worked with sex-trafficking victims, then expanded that work to the Marine Corps, the Army, and an orphanage in Romania.
records.speaker: Erika Kirk

appearances.snippet: It kind of grew into something more global. I was living in China and doing a lot of work with the victims from sex trafficking and then began to phase that into working with the Marine Corps and the Army and then was able to work with a orphanage in Romania. to help sustain them during their winter seasons and giving them more clothing items or tangible items rather than just money.

verification.notes: Public transcript context records Erika Kirk making the China, trafficking-victim, military, and Romania claims. Independent reporting corroborates her charity's Romanian orphanage gifts and a partnership involving U.S. service members, but could not verify the claimed China residence/sex-trafficking work; the Marine Corps and Army did not confirm the partnerships when asked.

records.text: Lori Frantzve established Everyday Heroes Like You in April 2009, and its filing described it as a faith-based organization raising funds and developing programs for vulnerable children.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: In 2009, Lori Frantzve is going to establish Everyday Heroes Like You in April. ... In her filing, she will claim that it is a faith-based organization that is raising funds and developing programs for vulnerable children.

verification.notes: Arizona corporate records show Everyday Heroes Like You was incorporated in December 2007, with Erika Frantzve listed as president/CEO and Lori Frantzve as statutory agent; IRS-derived data shows tax-exempt status in 2009. This contradicts the claim that Lori established it in April 2009, while the charitable mission description is broadly consistent with later public profiles.

appearances.snippet: We run a company and that's how I was able to formulate my nonprofit and that's what also made me change my major because originally I was business.

records.text: Lori Frantzve established the Everyday Heroes foundation, from which the Romanian Angels Project emerged to work with the military in Romania helping orphans.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Lori Frantzve established the Everyday Heroes Foundation, which was supposed to help children in need. ... what spun out from Lori's charity was the Romanian Angels Project ... they worked with the military in Romania to help orphans.

verification.notes: The project and military-orphanage portions are supported, but the founder attribution is not. In a contemporaneous first-person interview, Erika Frantzve identified herself as the founder of Everyday Heroes Like You and said its Romanian Angels project teamed with the U.S. Marine Corps to jointly sponsor an orphanage in Constanta. Romanian local reporting likewise says Romanian Angels began in 2012 after Erika visited the Antonio placement center and documents American military participation. These sources contradict the claim that Lori Frantzve established the foundation.
